core_meaning.short_meaning: Fragrant wild lavender; companion Khuzaymah ibn Thabit (Dhu al-Shahadatayn).
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Khuzaymah (خُزَيْمَة) is a historic Arabic masculine name meaning 'delicate fragrant blossom' or 'a string of precious pearls'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Khuzaymah ibn Thabit al-Ansari, whom the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ uniquely honored with the title 'Dhu al-Shahadatayn' (He whose witness equals two men).
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive of khuzāmā (wild lavender) or referring to the careful stringing of beads, denoting order, fragrance, and precision.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root kh-z-m denotes stringing items harmoniously or refers to the sweet-scented desert lavender. In the prophetic era, Khuzaymah ibn Thabit bore testimony in a transaction where the Prophet ﷺ bought a horse; because of his profound truthfulness, the Prophet ﷺ decreed that his testimony alone was equivalent to that of two upright witnesses.
